---
title: "Walking Bass Generator"
toc: true
description: "Make a walking bass line over any changes (blues, ii–V–I, rhythm changes, a minor cycle, or your own), with chromatic runs, scale runs, jumps, enclosures, ghost notes and triplets you can turn up or down; see it in bass clef, hear it with a swing band, and send it to the Backing Track."

## Send to the Backing Track

<div class="wb-row">
<button type="button" id="wb-send-exact" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary">Band plays this exact line</button>
<button type="button" id="wb-send-dev" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary">Band walks with these devices</button>
</div>
<p id="wb-send-note" class="wb-check" aria-live="polite"></p>

The first button sends the line note for note: every chorus is written out as one long form, so the Backing Track plays it once through. Change the key or the changes there and it goes back to walking on its own. The second sends the changes and the device settings: the Backing Track's bassist makes up new lines with them, chorus after chorus.

## How it works

The bassist is the band's own (the Backing Track's "Walking with devices" line). Each bar starts on the chord's root
when the chord changes, and the last beat leads into the next bar's root. In a 4/4 bar with one chord, a device may
build the whole bar instead of the usual step-by-step search. *Device bars* is the share of bars where that happens; the
four sliders under it say how often each device is chosen. Examples (from the handout, as `bass.js` describes them):

- **Chromatic**: the root, then semitones running into the next root. F G A♭ A | B♭
- **Scalar**: down (or up) the chord's scale, the last step chromatic. F E♭ D C | B♭
- **Jump**: one leap of a 4th to a 6th inside the bar, then an approach note. F G A D | C (into C7)
- **Enclosure**: the next root's neighbours above and below before it lands. over C7 into A7: C A B♭ A♭ | A

Two ornaments may go on any walked bar:

- **Ghost notes**: a beat split into two swung eighths, the second barely played. Drawn with an x head.
- **Triplets**: beat 1 as a triplet falling down the chord (root, 5th, 3rd below). F C A, then beat 2.

*Variation* lets the band vary the rest of its playing more. The *Seed* makes the same line every time; *New line*
picks another seed. Under the score a check reads the ABC back: every bar must hold four beats and every drawn pitch must be the
one played.

The theory and more examples: [Walking Bass Lines](/lessons/walking-bass-lines.html).
